claims.text: A machine-learning model trained on DFT-derived local vibrational and electronic density-of-states descriptors can predict lattice and electronic thermal conductivity separately for HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed model can accurately predict the two thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr will be nearly equal.
From 300 to 1200 K, the lattice thermal conductivity will be approximately 30% below conventional Debye-based estimates.
The proposed approach will reduce prediction error by approximately a factor of two relative to earlier analytical models.
The model is applicable to both defect-free HfNbTaTiZr and a variant containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
The model is applicable over 50–1200 K.
Training on oxygen-containing configurations will capture the relevant configurational disorder in oxygen-contaminated HfNbTaTiZr.
Local bonding fluctuations and lattice distortions influence phonon dispersion.
Local bonding fluctuations and lattice distortions influence electron-scattering rates.
DFT-derived atomic-scale descriptors can represent the local distortions and bonding fluctuations relevant to transport.
Machine learning can interpolate complex correlations between chemical disorder and transport properties from local structural and electronic descriptors.
The descriptor-based model permits separate extraction of temperature-dependent lattice and electronic conduction without using a single Debye temperature.
Earlier approaches generally rely on one Debye temperature and conflate electronic and phononic thermal-conductivity contributions.
Prediction deviations may occur outside 50–1200 K or at impurity concentrations and defect densities substantially different from those represented in training.
Ab initio molecular dynamics can be used to train machine-learned force fields that are subsequently coupled to Green–Kubo calculations of thermal conductivity.
DFT-derived electronic states can be coupled to a linearized Boltzmann transport equation to calculate electronic thermal conductivity.
Models of high-entropy-alloy transport should be compared with experimental data to assess their validity.
The proposed combination of time-domain thermoreflectance and neutron or inelastic X-ray scattering can decisively decouple electronic and lattice thermal-conductivity contributions.

contradictions.description: The baseline broadly characterizes earlier approaches as conflating electronic and phononic contributions, but one cited record explicitly describes calculating electronic thermal conductivity separately from DFT electronic states using Boltzmann transport.
